TA0017.title: Criminal Organizations
TA0017.description:
Illicit-market organizations are profit-driven criminal gangs that divide labor around specific monetization chains. Unlike loose individual actors, they typically split roles across card sellers, account sellers, task runners, technicians, and money launderers, covering the full chain from account supply and attack-tool development to automated execution and cash-out. Common monetization models include marketing abuse, traffic inflation, fake registration, account takeover, credential stuffing, telecom fraud, and cross-border gambling.

Technical roles inside the organization build or procure SMS-receiving platforms, proxy pools, device-farm control, protocol scripts, and trojan cheats (AT0001/AT0004/AT0008/AT0026 etc.); operations roles dispatch bulk accounts and devices to execute tasks; finance roles launder proceeds via money-laundering gangs (TA0014). Their scaled, specialized operation lets them launch concentrated attacks against platform campaigns, risk-control rules, and new business scenarios, making them the primary driver of marketing fraud (R0005), traffic inflation (R0008), account takeover (R0030), and fake registration (R0043), and they routinely collaborate upstream and downstream with malware developers (TA0012) and money-laundering gangs (TA0014).
